import { Aside } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

A component app runs on its group's leader, and its writes are the log's: no
other node replays them. So a rule about who may write is a check in the method,
before anything is written. Two layers enforce it:

1. **The node**, from the method's attributes in the ABI, before the app runs.
2. **The app**, with `guards` and `env::caller()`, inside the method.

## What the node enforces

| Attribute | The node refuses |
| --- | --- |
| none | Callers who are not signed in (`401`). |
| `#[app::public]` | Nothing: anyone may call it on a public app, optionally rate-limited (`rate = "10/min"`). |
| `#[app::confirm]` | A call without a fresh passkey assertion. |
| `#[app::allow(system)]` | Only the node itself calls it (timers imply it). |
| `#[app::allow(app = "<id>")]` | Cross-app calls from any other app. |
| `#[app::allow(action)]` | Anyone but the app's own actions. |

A method with no attribute still admits any signed-in account the node lets
reach the app. Membership of the app's org is the app's to check.

## Guards: the org role

```rust
pub fn set_user_simple(&mut self, value: String) -> app::Result<()> {
    guards::require_member()?;
    self.user_simple.set(&value)?;
    Ok(())
}
```

`guards::require_member()` and `guards::require_admin()` return the caller's
account, or fail with `LoginRequired` (not an account: public, system or
another app) or `Forbidden` (below the role). For anything else, match on the
caller yourself, as `apps/permissions-showcase` does:

```rust
use calimero_sdk::env::Caller;

fn caller() -> app::Result<String> {
    match env::caller() {
        Caller::Account(a) | Caller::ApiKey { account: a, .. } => Ok(a),
        _ => Err(AppError::login_required()),
    }
}
```

`env::org_role(&account)` gives `Guest`, `Member`, `Admin` or `Owner` (ordered);
`env::in_team(&account, team)` checks a team.

## Write rules as data shapes

Each rule below is a key layout plus a check, all from the component apps in
`apps/` of core.

| Rule | Shape |
| --- | --- |
| **Only the author edits it** | Key the row by `(author, id)` with the author taken from the caller, never from an argument. Nobody can name another's row. |
| **Write once** | Key by `(…, author)` and refuse when the row exists (`AlreadyWritten`); offer no edit or remove. |
| **Moderated** | Never edited; removal checks the caller against a `moderators` table the owner seeded in `init`. |
| **Each account's own value** | `PerUser<T>`: `set`/`get`/`remove` act on the caller's account; `get_for(account)` reads another's. |
| **Content-addressed, never changed** | `Frozen<T>`: `insert` returns the hash and whether it was new; equal content stores nothing. |
| **Fixed at creation** | Write it in `#[app::init]` and expose no method that writes it. |

```rust
/// Sets `key` in the caller's own nested map.
pub fn set_user_nested(&mut self, key: String, value: String) -> app::Result<()> {
    let account = guards::require_member()?;
    self.user_nested.insert(&(account.clone(), key.clone()), &value)?;
    Ok(())
}
```

<Aside type="caution">
  Take identity from `env::caller()` or a guard, never from an argument: an
  argument is whatever the client sent.
</Aside>

## Test it

The SDK's harness runs the real component with an org of your choosing, so a
refusal is a test away ([Testing](/core/build/testing/)):

```rust
let mut t = TestApp::new(component, Org::new().admins(["ada"]).members(["bob"]).guests(["eve"]), T0);
assert!(t.as_("eve").call("setUserSimple", json!({ "value": "x" })).is_err());
```
